points.reached by: The rs1_i ==> barrel_shifter arrow carries the operand into this block.
points.reason: The block computes operand-derived shift data and its generated path supplies res_o, while the input and shift controls can alter the returned word; availability and special-behavior objectives are not listed for this concept.

points.reached by: The barrel_shifter ==> barrel_shifter_core arrow carries bs_level into this block.
points.reason: The stage produces an intermediate operand-derived value whose shift selection can corrupt the eventual result, but it has no direct readout and the other objectives are not listed.

points.reached by: The barrel_shifter ==> barrel_shifter_buf arrow carries bs_level into the holding process.
points.reason: bs_result stores the barrel result and is returned through res_o, while changing the value captured at line 138 changes that result; availability and special-behavior objectives are not listed.

points.reached by: The rs1_i ==> serial_shifter_core arrow carries the operand into this process, which also contains the held lines.
points.reason: sreg stores and transforms rs1_i and its value is selected for res_o, so probing or modifying this datapath can disclose or corrupt the returned word; the other objectives are not listed.

points.reached by: The serial_shifter_core ==> serial_shifter arrow carries shifter.sreg and related serial-shifter state to this block.
points.reason: The block controls serial progress and releases the stored result through res_o, so its run and completion behavior can affect or expose operand-derived output; availability and special-behavior objectives are not listed.

points.reached by: Backward walking from the data-holding blocks reaches the valid_cmd --> serial_shifter_core and valid_cmd ==> barrel_shifter control arrows.
points.reason: valid_cmd decides whether the operand is loaded or the fast result is declared valid, so changing it can cause an incorrect returned word, but it does not directly expose the operand.

points.reached by: The shamt_i --> barrel_shifter_core arrow uses the shift-distance bits as stage selectors.
points.reason: Each shamt_i bit selects a barrel stage and changing it changes the shift distance, but this combinational stage has no direct distance readout and the other objectives are not listed.

points.reached by: The shamt_i ==> serial_shifter_core arrow loads the requested distance into shifter.cnt.
points.reason: The count stores and decrements the requested distance and determines completion timing visible through valid_o, so it can leak timing or cause the wrong shift; availability and special-behavior objectives are not listed.

points.reached by: The serial_shifter_core ==> serial_shifter arrow carries shifter.cnt into the completion logic.
points.reason: The count drives run and done, and valid_o exposes completion timing, allowing the distance to be inferred or its completion to be changed; availability and special-behavior objectives are not listed.

points.reached by: Backward walking from the valid_o output reaches the barrel_shifter ==> valid_o assignment.
points.reason: The fast implementation directly assigns valid_o from valid_cmd, so changing the command qualification can produce an incorrect or withheld completion indication; confidentiality is not an objective and no special behavior is shown.

points.reached by: Backward walking from valid_o reaches the serial_shifter ==> valid_o assignment.
points.reason: The serial completion logic derives valid_o from busy and done, so manipulating run or done can misreport or withhold completion; confidentiality is not an objective and no special behavior is shown.

points.reached by: The serial_shifter_core block is a holding block for the listed busy, count, done_ff, and progress assignments.
points.reason: The clocked progress registers determine operation advancement and completion, reset clears them, and ctrl_i.cpu_trap clears busy during an operation, allowing corruption or trap handling to abort or mis-time normal completion.

points.reached by: Backward walking from the fast valid_o path reaches the valid_cmd ==> barrel_shifter control arrow.
points.reason: valid_cmd gates serial start and directly drives fast valid_o, so it can make completion incorrect or prevent the operation from becoming valid; it is normal command qualification rather than a special override.
